Most of this page is set in a font that says what each of its glyphs is. A few words are not, and neither are some parts of words, such as the middle of recovery or the end of glyphs. The reader has to place each of them by the text around it.

A line can hold two such words, and a number like 1234 too. A sign set alone, as in $ 5, is one glyph that nothing around it names.

The rest of the page is ordinary text, so that the page reads as one with text on it and not as one to read whole. A page set in a font with no values throughout is read as a scan is, and its text replaced; a page like this one keeps its text, and only the glyphs it cannot name are read off the page. That is the case this page is for: a document whose fonts mostly say what they draw, with a few words that do not, which is how most such documents come. The words around each one are what place it, and the reading is taken only where they agree with it.
